symptom: `column (Attribute: "MyModule"."AssocA_2"/"MyModule"."AssocB_2"/"NId")` in a Data grid 2 over a junction entity failed `mxcli check` with MDL-WIDGET34 "Attribute: &{…} is not an attribute binding MDL can store" plus MDL-WIDGET42 "cannot hold the expression" (mxcli 0.25.0, Mendix 11.12.4).
cause: Same root as the 2026-10-11 qualified-association-hop finding: attributePathV3 took only bare identifiers between slashes, so module-qualified hops fell through to `keyword COLON expression` and parsed as a division. Already fixed by 05a05aad, which shipped after the 0.25.0 the reporter ran; its tests pinned two qualified hops at the parser but only one hop at the builder.
fix: No code change. Added the reported shape as tests at the check layer (the issue's script verbatim through visitor.Build + validateWidgetTree) and at the builder (two qualified hops -> Attribute MyModule.AssocB.NId with two IndirectEntityRef steps, equal to the bare spelling), plus a bug-test MDL. mx check on 11.12.4: 0 errors with and without widget normalisation.
insight: Before fixing a report, check whether HEAD already passes the reporter's script verbatim and build the commit before the suspected fix as a control: here the pre-fix binary reproduced the exact `&{…}` WIDGET34 text, which proves the match rather than assuming it from the error code. A 'two hops' parser case does not cover the builder walking two hops — pin each layer with the reported depth. Wrong turn to skip: the reporter's entities are external (OData); the path resolution is the same for persistent entities, so the repro does not need an OData service. Side observation: DESCRIBE of a snippet data view sourced from a snippet parameter prints no DataSource although the BSON stores SnippetParameter.
